'''John Colin Stillwell''' (born 1942) is an Australian [[mathematician]] on the faculties of the [[University of San Francisco]] and [[Monash University]].<ref name="usfca.edu">{{Cite web|url=https://www.usfca.edu/faculty/john-stillwell|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20100929112357/http://www.usfca.edu/facultydetails.aspx?id=4294969536|url-status=dead|title=John Stillwell &#124; University of San Francisco|archivedate=29 September 2010|website=www.usfca.edu}}</ref>

==Biography==

He was born in [[Melbourne, Australia]] and lived there until he went to the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] for his doctorate.<ref name="usfca.edu"/>  He received his PhD from MIT in 1970, working under [[Hartley Rogers, Jr]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=44223|title=John Stillwell - The Mathematics Genealogy Project|website=www.mathgenealogy.org}}</ref> who had himself worked under [[Alonzo Church]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=8021|title=Hartley Rogers, Jr. - The Mathematics Genealogy Project|website=www.mathgenealogy.org}}</ref> From 1970 until 2001, he taught at Monash University back in Australia and in 2002 began teaching in [[San Francisco]].<ref name="usfca.edu"/>

==Honors==
In 2005, Stillwell was the recipient of the [[Mathematical Association of America]]'s prestigious [[Chauvenet Prize]] for his article "The Story of the [[120-cell|120-Cell]],"<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/200101/fea-stillwell.pdf|title=Story of the 120-Cell}}</ref> [[Notices of the AMS]], January 2001, pp.&nbsp;17&ndash;24.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.maa.org/Awards/chauvent.html|title=MAA awards page|access-date=5 January 2008|archive-date=31 May 2000|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20000531094216/http://www.maa.org/awards/chauvent.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2012, he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 5 August 2013.</ref>

==Works==
===Books===
Stillwell is the author of many textbooks and other books on mathematics including:
*''Classical Topology and Combinatorial Group Theory'', 1980, {{isbn|0-387-97970-0}}
** [https://books.google.com/books?id=WtcRBwAAQBAJ 2012 pbk reprint of 1993 2nd edition] {{isbn|978-0-387-97970-0}}
*''Mathematics and Its History'', 1989, [https://books.google.com/books?id=YfDiBwAAQBAJ pbk reprint of 2nd edition 2002]; 3rd edition 2010, {{isbn|0-387-95336-1}}<ref>{{cite web|author=Wilders, Richard J.|date=August 16, 2010|title=Review of ''Mathematics and Its History'' by John Stillwell|website=MAA Reviews, Mathematical Association of America|url=https://old.maa.org/press/maa-reviews/mathematics-and-its-history}}</ref>
*''Geometry of Surfaces'', 1992, {{isbn|0-387-97743-0}};<ref>{{cite journal|title=Review of ''Geometry of Surfaces'' by John Stillwell|journal=Choice|first=J.|last=McCleary|via=Library Catalog, University of Chicago|url=https://catalog.lib.uchicago.edu/vufind/Record/4841050/Reviews}}</ref> [https://books.google.com/books/about/Geometry_of_Surfaces.html?id=jksOBwAAQBAJ 2012 pbk reprint of 1st edition]
*''Elements of Algebra: Geometry, Numbers, Equations'', 1994,<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Freudenburg|first=Gene|date=1 January 1996|title=Review of Elements of Algebra|jstor=2975124|journal=[[The American Mathematical Monthly]]|volume=103|issue=2|pages=186–189|doi=10.2307/2975124}}</ref> {{isbn|0-387-94290-4}}
*''Numbers and Geometry'', 1998, {{isbn|0-387-98289-2}}
*''Elements of Number Theory'', 2003, {{isbn|0-387-95587-9}}
*[https://books.google.com/books?id=I1QPQic_PxwC ''The Four Pillars of Geometry''], 2005,<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Hunacek|first=Mark|date=1 January 2007|title=Review of The Four Pillars of Geometry|jstor=40378384|journal=[[The Mathematical Gazette]]|volume=91|issue=521|pages=375–378|doi=10.1017/S0025557200181951|s2cid=164895282 }}</ref> {{isbn|0-387-25530-3}}
*[https://books.google.com/books?id=HUFZDwAAQBAJ ''Yearning for the Impossible: The Surprising Truths of Mathematics''], 2006, {{isbn|1-56881-254-X}}<ref>{{cite journal|author=Biss, Daniel|authorlink=Daniel Biss|title=Review: ''Yearning for the Impossible'', by John Stillwell|journal=Notices of the AMS|date=June–July 2007|volume=54|issue=6|pages=722–723|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/200706/tx070600722p.pdf}}</ref>
*[https://books.google.com/books?id=SuR5OAgxyDIC ''Naive Lie Theory''], 2008, {{isbn|0-387-98289-2}}<ref>{{cite web|author=Stenger, Allen|date=October 6, 2008|title=Review of ''Naive Lie Theory'' by John Stillwell|website=MAA Reviews, Mathematical Association of America|url=https://old.maa.org/press/maa-reviews/naive-lie-theory}}</ref>
*[https://books.google.com/books?id=XvPRBQAAQBAJ ''Roads to Infinity''], 2010, {{isbn|978-1-56881-466-7}}
*''The Real Numbers: An Introduction to Set Theory and Analysis'', 2013, {{isbn|978-3319015767}}<ref>{{cite web|author=Stenger, Allen|date=February 5, 2014|title=Review of ''The Real Numbers: An Introduction to Set Theory and Analysis'' by John Stillwell|website=MAA Reviews, Mathematical Association of America|url=https://old.maa.org/press/maa-reviews/the-real-numbers-an-introduction-to-set-theory-and-analysis}}</ref>
*[https://books.google.com/books/about/Elements_of_Mathematics.html?id=xSqWjgEACAAJ ''Elements of Mathematics: From Euclid to Gödel''], 2016, {{isbn|978-0691171685}}<ref>{{cite web|author=Hunacek, Mark|date=May 12, 2016|title=Review of ''Elements of Mathematics: From Euclid to Gödel'' by John Stillwell|website=MAA Reviews, Mathematical Association of America|url=https://old.maa.org/press/maa-reviews/elements-of-mathematics-from-euclid-to-g-del}}</ref>
*''[[Reverse Mathematics: Proofs from the Inside Out]]'', 2018, {{isbn|978-0691177175}}
*''A Concise History of Mathematics for Philosophers'', 2019, {{isbn|978-1108610124}}
*''The Story of Proof: Logic and the History of Mathematics'', 2022, {{isbn|978-0691234366}}
